title: Memory shortage causing repricing of consumer electronics due to AI GPU demand
description: David Oks explains how AI data center growth is pushing HBM (high-bandwidth memory) allocation from 2% to 20% of wafer capacity by end of 2026. Since HBM consumes 3x more wafer capacity per GB than DDR/LPDDR, this is constraining consumer RAM production. Expected to impact sub-$100 smartphone market particularly hard.
author: Simon Willison (citing David Oks)

title: FTC settles charges over deceptive 'active listening' AI marketing claims
description: FTC required Cox Media Group and two other firms to pay nearly $1 million for falsely claiming their 'Active Listening' service used smart devices to listen to conversations for ad targeting. In reality, the service just resold email lists from other data brokers at markup. FTC clarified that clicking through terms of service does not constitute adequate consent for voice data collection.
author: Simon Willison

title: MOSS: Self-Evolution through Source-Level Rewriting in Autonomous Agent Systems
description: Research paper introducing MOSS, a system for autonomous agent self-evolution through source-level code rewriting. Enables agents to modify their own codebase to improve performance over time. Published on ArXiv 2026-05-22.
author: Qianshu Cai, Yonggang Zhang, et al.

title: Compiling Agentic Workflows into LLM Weights: Near-Frontier Quality at 100x Less Cost
description: Research paper demonstrates a technique to compile agentic workflow patterns directly into LLM weights, achieving near-frontier performance at two orders of magnitude lower computational cost. Published on ArXiv 2026-05-22.
author: Simon Dennis, Rivaan Patil, Kevin Shabahang, Hao Guo

title: Advancing Mathematics Research with AI-Driven Formal Proof Search
description: Large-scale collaboration demonstrating AI systems (including Aja Huang) advancing mathematics research through automated formal proof search. Represents significant progress in AI-assisted mathematical discovery. Published on ArXiv 2026-05-22.
author: George Tsoukalas, Anton Kovsharov, et al.

title: TerminalWorld: Benchmarking Agents on Real-World Terminal Tasks
description: New benchmark for evaluating AI agents on realistic terminal/command-line tasks. Addresses gap in agent evaluation for practical development workflows. Published on ArXiv 2026-05-22.
author: Zhaoyang Chu, Jiarui Hu, et al.

title: Is Capability a Liability? More Capable LLMs Make Worse Forecasts When It Matters Most
description: Research finding that more capable language models produce worse forecasts in high-stakes scenarios, suggesting a capability-reliability tradeoff. Published on ArXiv 2026-05-22.
author: Nick Merrill, Jaeho Lee, Ezra Karger

title: Datasette Agent: First release of extensible AI assistant for Datasette
description: Simon Willison announced Datasette Agent, a new extensible AI assistant for Datasette that integrates his LLM Python library (3 years in development) with Datasette. Features include 'View SQL query' buttons for charts, improved handling of truncated responses, and support for Datasette Agent plugins running in Fly Sprites sandbox.
author: Simon Willison

title: Anthropic paying SpaceX $1.25 billion per month for GPU compute capacity
description: SpaceX S-1 filing reveals Cloud Services Agreements with Anthropic for access to COLOSSUS and COLOSSUS II GPU compute capacity. Anthropic agreed to pay $1.25 billion per month through May 2029, with capacity ramping in May-June 2026 at reduced fees. Agreement terminable with 90 days notice.
author: Simon Willison

title: How fast is 10 tokens per second? Interactive simulation tool
description: Mike Veerman built an HTML app that simulates LLM token output speeds from 5/second to 800/second, helping developers understand what different token rates actually feel like in practice.
author: Simon Willison

title: Google I/O 2026: Gemini 3.5 Flash and Gemini Spark agent
description: Google released Gemini 3.5 Flash (general availability, skipping preview) and announced Gemini Spark, an OpenClaw competitor described as 'your personal AI agent' that connects natively with Google apps. Spark runs on Gemini 3.5 Flash and 'Antigravity'. Security approach: fully managed runtime with fresh isolated VMs per task, secure Agent Gateway with DLP policies. Concerns raised about prompt injection risks given sensitive data exposure.
author: Simon Willison

title: Lex Fridman Podcast #490: State of AI in 2026 - LLMs, Coding, Scaling Laws, China, Agents, GPUs, AGI
description: 4.5-hour comprehensive discussion with Nathan Lambert (machine learning researcher, post-training lead at Allen Institute for AI) and Sebastian Raschka (ML researcher and educator) covering the current state of AI in 2026. Topics include large language models, AI programming, scaling laws, AI development in China, AI agents, GPU infrastructure, AGI, technical breakthroughs, and open vs closed LLMs.
author: Lex Fridman with Nathan Lambert and Sebastian Raschka

title: Andrej Karpathy: 2026 will be the 'Slopacolypse' - AI now writes most of his code
description: At Sequoia AI Ascent 2026, Andrej Karpathy predicted that 2026 will be the 'Slopacolypse'. He noted that AI is now writing most of his code and he is 'starting to atrophy my ability to write code manually'. Noted that last year he coined 'vibe coding' but 'this year, he's never felt more behind as a programmer'. Reflects on rapid pace of AI advancement in 2026.
author: Andrej Karpathy

title: Gemini 3.5 Flash: More expensive, but Google plans to use it everywhere
description: Analysis of Google's Gemini 3.5 Flash release at Google I/O 2026. The model went straight to general availability and is being integrated across Google's product suite. Discusses pricing implications and Google's strategy.
author: Simon Willison

title: The last six months in LLMs: Five-minute lightning talk from PyCon US 2026
description: Simon Willison's annotated slides from a five-minute lightning talk covering recent developments in LLMs over the past six months. Provides a quick overview of the rapidly evolving landscape.
author: Simon Willison

title: Andrej Karpathy: LLMs are about more than just speeding up existing workflows
description: Andrej Karpathy tweeted about how LLMs represent a fundamental shift beyond just accelerating existing workflows like coding. He emphasized the consolidation happening in AI fields (vision, speech, natural language, reinforcement learning) into unified architectures. Discusses how this consolidation is creating new possibilities that didn't exist before.
author: Andrej Karpathy
